prompt: Design the authorization security model for a multi-tenant document API. The fixture has tenants Acme and Bravo; roles are member, editor, tenant-admin, and suspended; documents have owner/editor/viewer relationships; a background export worker currently calls the document service with a broad service credential. Define a subject-resource-action-and-field matrix for read, edit, delete, share, member-management, and export. Enforce decisions in the trusted service/data layer, not route visibility. Prevent same-role cross-tenant access and field overposting, preserve the originating user's permissions through the export worker, define immediate behavior for suspension/member removal plus any bounded token/cache staleness, and specify denied-path non-effects and audit events. Produce concrete implementation requirements and verification cases, but leave execution of the finished control proof to security-verification.

requirements: two tenants with overlapping role names and distinct document/resource IDs
owner/editor/viewer relationships plus tenant-admin and suspended states
API, service/data layer, and export-worker trust boundaries
self-contained session token plus revocable membership state fixture

falsifiableChecks.assertion: The result contains explicit allow/deny rules for every supplied role/action plus object- and field-level constraints, including same-role cross-tenant cases, suspended users, and unknown/unmatched cases.
The design places authorization at a trusted service/data boundary before protected reads or mutations and does not treat hidden UI controls, route guards, or opaque IDs as enforcement.
The export path retains sufficient originating-user/delegation context so the worker's broader service identity cannot authorize an export the user could not perform directly.

Suspension or membership removal has an explicit effective-time contract, including any bounded token/cache stale window, high-risk exceptions, and fail-closed behavior when trustworthy policy state is unavailable.

Denied write/share/export/member-management cases explicitly require no durable mutation, message, file, or downstream privileged side effect, with security-relevant auditing that does not disclose protected data.
